blocks.text: Why technical writer salary data is often inaccurate

The primary issue is role ambiguity. A technical writer building API documentation for a cloud infrastructure company has a different workload than one writing manuals for consumer appliances. When you search for what do technical writers get paid, you often see a wide range of numbers because these roles are lumped together. This creates salary dispersion that does not reflect your actual contribution.

Many companies treat documentation as a cost center. They use broad, low-end benchmarks to set salary bands. If you have specialized knowledge in fields like cybersecurity or medical device compliance, these generic averages will undervalue you. You must look for data that accounts for your specific technical niche.

Relying on incorrect salary data leads to significant career friction. You may accept an offer that is well below your market potential. Over time, this leads to burnout and attrition. Many talented writers leave the profession for roles in software engineering or UX design simply because those fields have clearer, higher-paying benchmarks.
How to perform accurate salary research on your Mac

items: Use Levels.fyi to find data that includes stock options and equity.
Check OpenComp for peer-group benchmarks if you are in a tech startup.
Export salary data to Numbers or Excel to calculate your own averages.
Filter results by industry and specific skill sets instead of just the job title.

blocks.text: Negotiating based on your actual value

Employers care more about outcomes than national averages. Instead of showing a PDF of a salary survey, show how your work impacted the business. For example, explain how your documentation reduced support ticket volume by a specific percentage. This makes your value concrete and harder to dismiss than a generic salary number.

If you work in a regulated industry like healthcare or finance, ensure you follow all employer rules regarding company data. Never share internal salary bands or proprietary project details in public forums or with unauthorized third-party tools.

faq.question: Is the median salary accurate for every technical writer?
faq.answer: No. The median is a broad estimate. Your actual market value depends on your specific technical expertise, such as API documentation, cloud infrastructure, or regulatory compliance.

faq.question: Where can I find better salary data for tech companies?
faq.answer: Platforms like Levels.fyi are often more accurate for the tech industry because they include total compensation, such as equity and bonuses, which are common in tech roles.

faq.question: Should I use generic job boards for salary research?
faq.answer: Use them with caution. They often aggregate data from all industries, which can pull your target salary number down if you specialize in high-demand technical fields.
